thread:
ash: heads-up: ran a short bring-up of ceres-40b quantized to int4 with our speculative-two-branch decoder on the retrieval-QA benchmark. summary: latency win ~18% but downstream exact-match drops on short numeric answers. digging.

 ravi: can you share the exact decode params and model build?

 ash: build "ceres-40b-int4-q1"; speculative branches=2, branch-cutoff-p=0.015, kv_prefetch=true, prefill_len=512, batch=4. run id: 6981122334-exp-5012.

 maya: curious if you used shard-level quant vs block-wise. blockwise tends to keep exponent fidelity.

 ash: blockwise-quant enabled. still seeing date/number flips. looks like off-by-decade in a handful of cases.

 sam: are the failures concentrated in short-answer templates (e.g., "Year X") or multi-hop?

 ash: mostly short canonical answers. example: prompt -> "In which year did the treaty signings conclude?" expected "1804"; speculative -> "1884". token IDs around numbers are stable but logits show near-tie.

 ravi: speculation: int4 reduces softmax resolution; speculative merges amplify tiny argmax flips. two small asks: (1) dump top-5 logits pre/post branch-merge for N worst cases, (2) run same decode but with kv_prefetch=false.

 ash: adding both. command used: ```python runner.py --model ceres-40b-int4-q1 --decode speculative --branches 2 --merge-mode fork_merge --dump-logits 50 --kv-prefetch true```

 maya: also try "high-precision-prefix" trick: keep prefix KV in fp16 and rest int4. point is to preserve earlier context distribution.

 ash: queued high-precision-prefix run as exp-5015. ops-bot: any ETA on spare A10s for these small runs?

 ops-bot: queued by ash. est start 2026-04-02T09:10Z. allocated pool: research-a10-small. est runtime 25m per job.

 sam: quick mitigation idea: apply post-hoc rerank using fp32 scoring on candidate beam list (no regen). cheap and often recovers exact-match for numeric answers. can we measure cpu overhead?

 ravi: measure with a small sample first. if rerank cost is ~<1.5x then acceptable.

 ash: ran rerank-only (exp-5016): rerank on 200 examples recovered ~85% of lost EM. cpu cost measured ~+30% p90 on postprocess.

 maya: good. long-term fix: either increase int precision in exponent or change merge policy to prefer main-branch logits when top1 gap is small. we can add a confidence gating: only spawn branch if top1-top2 < delta.

 sam: value of gating: reduces number of speculative forks for confident tokens, preserves latency for easy cases. try delta=0.08 then 0.05.

 ash: queued gating runs exp-5017 (delta=0.08) & exp-5018 (delta=0.05).

 ravi: also add control: same speculative config but model int8 (ceres-40b-int8) to confirm quant bitwidth is culprit.

 ash: int8 run exp-5019 queued.

 ops-bot: job updates: exp-5012 complete, exp-5015 queued, exp-5016 complete, exp-5017 running on research-a10-03, exp-5019 queued. logs available at s3://redwood-evals/6981122334/*

 maya: please post 5 worst examples (with logits dump) here once done. also include tokenizer mapping for numeric tokens; sometimes tokenization splits numbers weirdly and quant noise hits middle tokens.

 ash: good point. found one case where "1804" tokenized to ["18","04"] which likely magnified flip. adding tokenization-aware analysis.

 sam: next steps summary: (1) rerank patch as short-term mitigation, (2) gating + high-precision-prefix as medium-term, (3) kernel/quant fix upstream as long-term.

 ash: agreed. will collect aggregated metrics across 5k query sample and drop summary + run ids. leaning to gate+fprefix for enabling speculative by default.

 ops-bot: final update: exp-5017 complete, metrics pushed to dashboard: latency -18% vs greedy, EM -3.2 absolute for int4-speculative; gating delta=0.08 recovers ~1.7 EM.

 maya: thanks 44d please link the s3 dumps and close the issue when we have kernel repro.
